items.title: ClueFlow: Learning Long-Horizon Search through Attributed Research-State Transitions
items.summary_1line: Long-horizon search requires agents to acquire relevant evidence and integrate it into an evolving research state. Existing methods maintain research states to guide exploration or assign turn-level progress signals,...
items.editor_note: Attributes search progress to research-state transitions instead of turn-level signals.

items.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning
items.summary_1line: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to...
items.editor_note: Couples memory with learned skills so decisions fit a bounded context.

items.title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
items.summary_1line: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task...
items.editor_note: Identifies conditions where fine-grained credit assignment fails to improve task performance.

editorial.tldr: A run of arXiv papers on how agents learn from their own trajectories. ClueFlow credits search steps by research-state transitions, and a memory-skill paper tackles lifelong learning under a bounded context window.
editorial.whats_new: A multimodal RL paper on video editing asks when fine-grained credit assignment helps agent training and when it fails to improve task performance.
editorial.why_it_matters: Credit assignment and memory design determine how agents improve from experience, which affects how you build training signals and context management for long-horizon agents.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adding per-step rewards to an agent RL setup, run an ablation against outcome-only rewards on your own tasks.
